steps.what: 26. Every hook is a virtual no-op on AbstractModel (returning Task.CompletedTask or the unmodified value), so the dispatcher calls EVERY listener unconditionally and 'does not implement' equals 'implements as identity' (AbstractModel.cs:199-2440)
steps.rationale: The sim dispatches duck-typed -- `if hasattr(l, '<hook>')` (hooks.py:62 and the same line in all 66 dispatchers), stated as intentional in the module docstring ('Dispatch is duck-typed: a hook only calls listeners that define a matching method'). The observable is identical whenever the method names agree, because a C# no-op override and an absent Python method both contribute nothing; the only difference is a maintenance one (a misspelled hook name is a silent no-op in the sim and a compile error in C#), which is why test/test_hook_order.py's `trace` helper raises AttributeError on an unknown hook name.

steps.rationale: The sim collapses `bool Try(out v)` into `v = f(v)` (hooks.py:196-201 and the other chain hooks), which produces the identical value because a C# listener that returns false leaves modifiedCost == originalCost. The one thing the boolean carries that the fold cannot is membership of the out-modifiers list, and that consequence is recorded separately at step 38 rather than duplicated here.

steps.what: 35. Predicate family, AND with first-False short-circuit, several with an out preventer/modifier naming the vetoing listener -- ShouldAddToDeck (2084), ShouldAfflict (2101), ShouldAllowAncient (2116), ShouldAllowHitting (2131), ShouldAllowMerchantCardRemoval (2146), ShouldAllowSelectingMoreCardRewards (2161), ShouldAllowTargeting (2176), ShouldDisableRemainingRestSiteOptions (2254), ShouldDraw (2269), ShouldGenerateTreasure (2316), ShouldGainStars (2331), ShouldPayExcessEnergyCostWithStars (2346), ShouldPlay (2361), ShouldProceedToNextMapPoint (2393), ShouldProcurePotion (2408), ShouldRefillMerchantEntry (2423), ShouldPowerBeRemovedOnDeath (2495)
steps.maps_to: hooks.py's predicates are the same AND-with-first-False short-circuit: should_die (588-594, with a preventer list out-param), should_remove_from_combat_after_death (607-611), should_clear_block (615-619), should_reset_energy (625-629), should_draw (638-642), should_flush_hand (648-652), should_allow_hitting (656-660), should_play_card (690-694), should_ethereal_trigger (698-702). The short-circuit makes the vetoer order-dependent, which is exactly why step 2's ordering is gap G2 (and turn_structure's G2). The missing preventer out-param matters at only one dispatcher this record owns, Hook.AfterPreventingDraw (1056-1067), whose sole implementer in the whole game is Fiddle.cs:39-43 and whose body is `Flash();` -- presentation only, so nothing observable is dropped.

steps.what: 36. Predicate family, OR with first-True short-circuit -- ShouldStopCombatFromEnding (2442-2452) and ShouldTakeExtraTurn (2457-2467)
steps.maps_to: hooks.py:667-671 should_take_extra_turn returns True on the first listener that does, matching Hook.cs:2459-2466 (its docstring says so). Both dispatchers are turn_structure's; the shape is recorded here because the seed fact's 'predicate short-circuits on any False' does not describe them.

steps.what: 37. Predicate family, OR with NO short-circuit -- `flag = flag || item.ShouldX(...)` calls every listener even after one returns true: ShouldForcePotionReward (2472-2480) and ShouldAllowFreeTravel (2485-2493)
steps.issue: The sim aggregates both with a short-circuiting `any(...)` generator (rewards.py:449: `any(relic.should_force_potion_reward(run, room_type) for relic in run.relics)`), so C# calls every listener where the sim stops at the first True and a later listener with a side effect would be skipped. DORMANT, evidence executed: each hook has exactly ONE implementer in the decompiled game outside the run-modifier set -- WhiteBeastStatue.cs for ShouldForcePotionReward and WingedBoots.cs for ShouldAllowFreeTravel (Modifiers/Flight.cs is the second and run modifiers are note N4's waiver) -- so no second listener exists to be skipped, and both implementers' predicates are side-effect free. Concrete trigger: a second ported implementer of either hook, or one whose predicate has a side effect.

steps.what: 38. Modifier-notification lists: chain/try-chain dispatchers with an `out modifiers` parameter add a listener only when its call actually CHANGED the value, and ModifyEnergyGain (1610-1618) / ModifyGoldGained (1630-1638) compare with an INTEGER cast so a sub-1 decimal change does not count; ModifyCardPlayCount (1376-1384), ModifyCardPlayResultPileTypeAndPosition (1396-1405) and ModifyCardBeingAddedToDeck (1350-1364) track it exactly. The caller then fires the matching AfterModifying* event over exactly that subset
steps.issue: hooks.py implements this mechanism for exactly one hook, modify_hp_lost (126-147, with after_modify_hp_lost at 149-154) -- damage_pipeline's site. The dispatchers this record owns have no modifiers list and no companion event: modify_energy_gain (210-215), modify_card_play_count (224-234), modify_card_play_result_pile (236-246), and the deck/reward ones have no sim counterpart at all. DORMANT for the card-play-count case by construction: the three ported AfterModifyingCardPlayCount listeners each consume their stack INSIDE the sim's modifier instead (powers.py:966-978 One-Two Punch, powers.py:3919-3928 Duplication, relics/throwing_axe.py:30-36 Throwing Axe, each with a source comment saying so), a deliberate compensation with the same observable. Concrete trigger: porting NoEnergyGainPower (the sole AfterModifyingEnergyGain implementer) or BowlerHat/Ectoplasm's AfterModifyingGoldGained legs, none of which is a sim listener on that hook today, and any future ported listener that must know it was outvoted.

steps.what: 39. Dispatcher-level guards outside the loop: ModifyEnergyCostInCombat returns originalCost untouched when it is negative (Hook.cs:1576-1579), ShouldPowerBeRemovedOnDeath returns true when power.Owner.CombatState == null (2497-2500), and the LocalContext.NetId early return of step 24
steps.maps_to: hooks.py:196-201 modify_card_energy_cost has no negative-cost arm, but its input cannot be negative: Card.energy_cost (cards/base.py:222-232) already returns max(0, base + delta), and that property is the only producer of the argument at every call site (combat.py:408, combat.py:701, env.py:88/94/140, previews.py:181). ShouldPowerBeRemovedOnDeath has no sim counterpart hook at all beyond should_remove_from_combat_after_death (a different predicate), and a sim Power always has an owner in a combat.

steps.what: 40. Event dispatchers return no value and ignore listener output entirely: no cancellation, no ordering feedback (the ~60 `await model.X(); model.InvokeExecutionFinished();` bodies)
steps.maps_to: hooks.py's event hooks are the same fire-and-forget walk (on_combat_start 267-269 through on_death 576-578); the sim likewise ignores return values.

steps.what: 41. Sim registry: HookSystem.__init__ holds one flat self._listeners list plus a self.combat back-reference (hooks.py:37-41)
steps.issue: gap G2 (cross-listener order): CombatState.cs:413-467 groups listeners PER CREATURE, allies before enemies, and within a player walks Powers -> Relics -> PotionSlots -> Orbs -> cards. The sim keeps one flat registration-order list (hooks.py:38,43-44) whose category order is History -> Cards -> Relics -> Potions -> Powers (combat.py:106-166, cmds.py:326) -- powers first in the game and LAST in the sim, cards last in the game and FIRST in the sim. LIVE and executed on Hook.ModifyEnergyCostInCombat: with CuriousPower(2) (CuriousPower.cs:12-32, powers.py:2883, applied by the ported Mad Science card) and Spiked Gauntlets (SpikedGauntlets.cs:27-39, relics/spiked_gauntlets.py:26-32, ported Tanx shrine) on a 1-cost Power card the game computes max(0,1-2)=0 then +1 = 1 and the sim computes 1+1=2 then max(0,2-2) = 0.

steps.what: 42. Sim registry: register() appends, unregister() is list.remove (identity, since no sim model defines __eq__) and raises ValueError when absent, which every caller wraps -- cmds.py:341-345, cmds.py:445-448, player.py:130-134, powers.py:89-92 (hooks.py:43-47)
steps.maps_to: C# has no register/unregister at all -- membership is structural (a power is a listener because it is in creature.Powers). The sim's explicit registry is the mechanism that produces gap G2's ordering; the register/unregister PRIMITIVES themselves are consistent with the game's reference semantics: identity-based, idempotent-safe, and every removal site mirrors a C# removal site (PowerCmd.Remove / power expiry -> cmds.py:341 and powers.py:89, a potion leaving the belt -> player.py:130, a card removed from combat -> cmds.py:445).

steps.what: 44. player.all_cards is hand + draw_pile + discard_pile + exhaust_pile (player.py:100-103), evaluated ONCE at combat start, so the card listener order is frozen for the combat
steps.issue: gap G1 (card listener order is per-pile and re-derived in C#, frozen at combat start in the sim): CombatState.cs:449-467 walks AllPiles = Hand, Draw, Discard, Exhaust, Play (PlayerCombatState.cs:70-80) on EVERY dispatch, so a card that moves pile moves position in the listener list. combat.py:124 registers player.all_cards once, in the fixed order hand+draw+discard+exhaust (player.py:100-103), and never reorders. DORMANT, evidence executed: an MRO-aware scan of the whole _CARD_CLASSES registry finds card classes implementing only six hooks, none able to observe cross-card order -- on_card_entered_combat (1: Stomp), on_card_exhausted (1: Drum of Battle), on_energy_spent (1: Stomp), on_player_turn_start (2: Bolas, Thrumming Hatchet, both self-only), on_player_turn_end (2: Howl from Beyond, Regret -- neither reads state the other writes), should_play_card (3: Clash, Enthralled, Normality -- an AND predicate whose sim dispatcher hooks.py:690-694 has no preventer out-param, so the vetoer's identity is unobservable). Concrete trigger: porting a card whose hook reads state another card's hook writes, or giving should_play_card a preventer out-param.

steps.what: 45. Every one of the 66 sim dispatchers is `for l in list(self._listeners): if hasattr(l, '<hook>'): l.<hook>(...)` -- the list() copy makes the walk a snapshot, so a listener registered during a dispatch is not called and one unregistered during it still is
steps.issue: gap G7 (no per-item liveness re-check, no IsActiveForHooks): C# yields `if (Contains(item))` LAZILY, per item (CombatState.cs:482-488), and Contains (549-599) drops any relic/potion/card/affliction/enchantment/orb whose HasBeenRemovedFromState is set or whose owner is not IsActiveForHooks (Player.cs:112,272,438,859-870); every sim dispatcher walks a `list(self._listeners)` snapshot with no re-check. DORMANT, evidence executed: the whole suite (2475 tests) re-run with HookSystem.register instrumented to flag any listener invoked while absent from _listeners yields exactly one hit, on_enemy_side_end -> IntangiblePower x10 (Nemesis removing Intangible mid-dispatch) -- and C# makes that same call, because the PowerModel arm of Contains (CombatState.cs:599) checks only Owner.CombatState != null and never that the power is still on its owner. Concrete trigger: a listener that melts a relic, discards a potion or removes a card from combat while a later listener of the same category is still pending in that dispatch.

steps.what: 46. The sim has no phase concept, no preventer for most predicates, no Contains re-check, no IsOverOrEnding gate, no per-listener choice context, and no run-level HookSystem (hooks.py in full)
steps.issue: gap G3 (missing Early/VeryEarly/Late phase passes): 24 of Hook.cs's 147 dispatchers run 2-4 complete listener passes and AbstractModel.cs declares 27 phase-suffixed hooks; hooks.py has one walk per hook and no phase concept at all (hooks.py:673-680 says so). BufferPower.cs:17-19 carries a source comment stating the Late phase is load-bearing. LIVE and executed: TangledPower's TryModifyEnergyCostInCombat (EARLY, powers.py:1486-1502, applied by the ported Vine Shambler, monsters/overgrowth/vine_shambler.py:42-43) and FreeAttackPower's TryModifyEnergyCostInCombatLate (LATE, FreeAttackPower.cs:14-40, powers.py:1133-1155, applied by the ported card Unrelenting, cards/unrelenting.py:40) both target Attacks -- the game always ends at cost 0, the sim ends at 1 when Free Attack was applied first and 0 when Tangled was.

guards.what: N1 -- multiplayer plumbing: PlayerChoiceContext push/pop (step 23), HookPlayerChoiceContext + AssignTaskAndWaitForPauseOrCompletion and the LocalContext.NetId early return (step 24), the grouped Task.WhenAll (step 25), the OrbQueue listener block (step 8), and MultiplayerScalingModel (step 10).
guards.rationale: Genuinely out of scope: one local player, one character (Ironclad), no orbs, no async pausing. Nothing a single-player run or replay can observe depends on any of it. The step-level waivers that cite N1 are steps 8, 23, 24, 25 and the MultiplayerScalingModel clause of step 10.

guards.what: N2 -- presentation and modding: InvokeExecutionFinished / the ExecutionFinished event (step 22) and the ModHelper.IterateAll*Subscribers tails (steps 13, 17).
guards.rationale: AbstractModel.cs:64-68 documents ExecutionFinished as 'a little unreliable, so you should only use it for UI things that can't be done any other way' -- presentation. ModHelper is the mod-loading extension point and the sim has no mod loader. Neither can change a single-player outcome.

guards.what: N3 -- CombatHistory is a sim-only listener, registered first (combat.py:111-112) so it observes every event before any relic or power. The game has no history listener: CombatManager.History is written by explicit calls (CardModel.cs:1930, 1956), not through the hook system.
guards.rationale: The observable is identical: CombatHistory only records, never mutates combat state, and registering it first is what makes the recording complete by the time a later listener reads it (relics/paels_eye.py:27-34 and relics/whispering_earring.py both scan it). Routing the recording through the listener list instead of through explicit call sites is a sim re-architecture with no behavioural consequence -- verified by reading every CombatHistory hook method, all of which only append entries.

guards.what: N4 -- Modifiers and BadgeModels as listeners (step 10; RunState.cs:573-574, CombatState.cs:470-477).
guards.rationale: Modifiers are custom/daily-run mutators loaded from save.Modifiers (RunState.cs:296, 344) and a standard run has none. BadgeModels ARE cloned into every run (RunState.cs:332), but BadgeModel.cs:3-9 states they exist to 'keep track of stats for badges' and an executed grep over src/Core/Models/Badges/ finds no badge overriding any Should*/Modify*/TryModify* hook -- they subscribe to events for meta-progression accounting only. Out of scope for the same reason ascension values are, and unable to change an in-run outcome even if they were in scope.

guards.what: N5 -- the run/combat delegation split: in combat a run-level dispatch visits deck cards first and then the whole combat list (steps 14-18), and the sim has two disjoint dispatch systems instead (HookSystem inside a combat, duck-typing over run.relics outside one).
guards.issue: gap N5 (no run-level listener list): RunState.cs:545-596 makes every deck card and its enchantment a run listener at all times, in combat and out, and delegates to the combat list when there is a child combat. The sim has no run-level HookSystem: run-scoped hooks are duck-typed directly over run.relics (relics/base.py:205-235) and a deck card is never a listener. DORMANT, evidence executed: the MRO-aware _CARD_CLASSES scan above finds no sim card class implementing a run-scoped hook at all (the six it implements are combat hooks). Concrete trigger: porting any CardModel that overrides AfterRoomEntered/AfterRewardTaken/ShouldAddToDeck or another run-level hook.

guards.what: N6 -- AbstractModel.ShouldReceiveCombatHooks (AbstractModel.cs:53-62) is abstract and 19 model classes override it, but a whole-source grep for reads finds ZERO consumers; the real filtering is structural (which lists IterateHookListeners walks) plus Contains.
guards.rationale: Documented-but-unread property. The sim has no counterpart and needs none: it performs the same filtering structurally, by choosing what to register. Recorded so a future reader does not mistake it for a missing gate. Executed: `grep -rn ShouldReceiveCombatHooks --include=*.cs .` over the whole decompiled tree returns only the abstract declaration and the 19 overrides, no reads.
